name: manual_fa9f7e
claim: Before any cross-repo guard-sync operation (or when a user asks 'is the other side actually behind, or does it have unique improvements?'), run the divergence checker proactively even when confident nothing has diverged -- treat empirical verification as the mandatory first step, not a defensive measure reserved for when drift is already suspected.

decisions.notes: 2026-08-09: asked whether PT's guard-sync-manifest-tracked scripts might have independent improvements not yet in orama canonical, before syncing/overwriting. Ran check-guard-sync-divergence.sh against the real repos (not scratch clones) and confirmed PASS -- PT had zero unique content, pure lag. The check cost seconds and closed the door on an entire class of accidental-clobber risk; the discipline of running it BEFORE forming a confident answer, not just when something already looks wrong, is the actual lesson -- confidence from reasoning about repo history is not a substitute for the empirical check the tooling already provides for free.
